The Nigerian Stock Exchange (NGX, officially Nigerian Exchange Group) is a leading integrated market infrastructure in Africa servicing the continent’s largest economy. The Exchange provides capital access to companies seeking to take advantage of the financial markets to fund their business expansion. Likewise, NGX provides its pool of domestic, regional, and international investors with an array of regulated securities to achieve their investment objectives. In March 2021, the erstwhile Nigerian Stock Exchange was demutualized from a member-owned not-for-profit entity into a shareholder-owned, profit making entity Nigerian Exchange Group Plc.

NGX publishes the benchmark, value-weighted All-Share Index (ASI), formulated in January 1984 with a base value of 100. The ASI tracks the general market movement of all listed equities on the Exchange, including those listed on the Growth Board, regardless of capitalization. Additional indices are the NGX30 and NGX50 which respectively track the top 30 and 50 companies in terms of market capitalization and liquidity. Both indices, in which only fully paid-up common shares are admitted, are weighted by adjusted market capitalization—the number of a company’s listed shares, multiplied by the closing price, and multiplied by a capping factor.

NGX TRADING SUMMARY FOR WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 23, 2026: At the end of today's trading session on the Nigerian Stock Exchange (NGX), a total of 1,590,482,405 shares in 49,736 deals, corresponding to a market value of NGN 45,800,165,497.43, were traded. Compared with the previous NGX trading day (Tuesday, September 22), today's data shows 90% improvement in volume, 6% decline in turnover, and 4% decline in deals. The current market capitalization of the Nigerian Stock Exchange is NGN 163.1 trillion (USD 123 billion).

In the aggregate, 132 NGX listed equities participated in trading, ending with 43 gainers and 20 losers. Eterna led the gainers with 10% share price appreciation closing at NGN 38.50 per share, followed by Thomas Wyatt Nigeria (+9.88%), Critical Minerals Financing Corp (+9.76%) and Haldane McCall (+9.7%). On the losing side, Caverton Offshore Support Group came out last with an end-of-day price depreciation of 9.09% at NGN 4.00 per share, followed by University Press (-9%), Coronation Insurance (-6.3%) and Veritas Kapital Assurance (-5.45%). Fortis Global Insurance recorded the highest volume of 860 million traded shares, followed by Fidelity Bank (171m), Guaranty Trust Holding (86.2m) and Dangote Sugar Refinery (36.5m).

Regarding the performance of NGX market indices, the benchmark NGX All-Share Index (ASI) inched up 576.36 (0.23%) points to close at 251,191.02, representing a one-week gain of 2.61%, a four-week gain of 5.24%, and an overall year-to-date gain of 61.42%. Other remarkable indices that performed were the NGX Top 30 Index (+0.21%; +2.65% 1WK; +62.95% YTD), NGX Insurance Index (+1.08%; +2.36% 1WK; -8.08% YTD), NGX Banking Index (+0.85%; +7.66% 1WK; +81.33% YTD), NGX Premium Index (+0.44%; +4.85% 1WK; +105.37% YTD), NGX Pension Index (+0.44%; +3.45% 1WK; +87% YTD), and NGX Consumer Goods Index (+0.17%; -0.53% 1WK; +2.95% YTD).

    Note that stock purchase depends on seller availability in as much it's a secondary market.
    It is 90 percent possible that at the price you place your request no seller was willing to sell at that price hence your broker was unable to buy until it get to a price seller was willing to sell.
